text: Strings are sequences of characters in quotes, single or double.
[cough] You can concatenate strings with plus, or repeat them with times.
The len function tells you how many characters a string has.
You can use single or double quotes interchangeably, and triple quotes let a string stretch across multiple lines.
Python gives strings a whole toolbox of methods — upper and lower change the case entirely.
And replace swaps out one piece of text for another, [sigh] returning a brand new string each time.
That's important — strings are immutable, so no method ever changes the original, it always hands you a fresh copy.
[sniff] The in keyword works on strings too, instantly telling you whether one piece of text appears inside another.
Strip removes leading and trailing whitespace, [chuckle] handy for cleaning up user input.
And split breaks a sentence into a list of individual words, using spaces by default.
